notes: Ranked by weekly_minutes_saved = saving_minutes_per_run x runs_per_week. saving_kind says what the minutes are: 'time-to-green' shortens how long a PR waits for all its checks; 'check-status-only' makes one check report sooner but the PR waits no less; 'main-publish' shortens the push-to-main publish run; 'runner-minutes' frees runners only (per-run figure is per avoided run). weekly_runner_minutes_saved is an approximate figure from the verdicts; negative means the change costs runner minutes. Wins overlap: the workspace paths filter removes most workspace e2e runs, so shard balancing and the tests-image pre-pull save less on workspace runs once it lands.

items.title: Every workspace PR runs the full all-suites e2e and smoke stack, though most touch nothing the stack uses
items.current_state: The pull_request trigger has no paths filter. Each workspace PR starts 4 runners (3 e2e shards plus k6 smoke), each with its own stack, running the 'all' scope. The check closes about 9-9.5 min after the push; tim-ci takes about 3 min, so e2e is the only thing holding tooling PRs open. Of PRs #131-#170, only 5 touched docker/, scripts/stack|ci, .github/, config/e2e* or repos.json.
items.proposal: Add a paths filter to the pull_request trigger only: docker/**, scripts/stack/**, scripts/ci/**, .github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml, .github/actions/**, config/e2e-tests-pr-scope.json, repos.json. Leave workflow_call and workflow_dispatch alone. To keep cross-repo coverage, also keep the trigger for feat/EUDPA-* and fix/EUDPA-* branches, or add openspec/** to the paths.
items.risk: A workspace PR on a cross-repo branch with no tests-repo PR is today the only all-suites run against that branch; most recent red runs were on such branches (feat/EUDPA-296). Keep the trigger for feature branches to avoid losing that signal. No required check exists, so a skipped run blocks nothing. The build loop already treats a merge that starts no workflow as green.
items.evidence: e2e-tests.yml lines 3-5 on origin/main (no paths:). 87 runs since 20 Oct, 75 not skipped. Runs 40484147231, 40481282780, 40471919627, 40439555493, 40397371456: slowest shard 8.1-9.4 min, smoke 4.3-5.3 min. gh api branches/main/protection returns 404. Verdict raised the saving from 6 to 7 min: on openspec/, workareas/ and docs PRs tim-ci does not run either, so the whole run goes.
items.dropped_reason: Sam, 27 Oct 2026: don't stop running tests; workspace PRs aren't a hot path.

items.title: The tests image is rebuilt from scratch on every PR push, and a slow apt mirror turns 1 build in 6 into a 20-minute wait before e2e can start
items.current_state: The shared publish-branch workflow builds with no-cache: true. Every build re-pulls base images, re-runs apt-get, the AWS CLI install, the ZAP copy and npm ci, then pushes every layer again. Whole workflow median 3.4 min. In 10 of 60 runs the amd64 apt layer stalled for 18-33 min. E2E is triggered by this workflow, so it waits for all of it.
items.proposal: Turn on BuildKit layer caching for branch builds and drop no-cache: true there. Use type=registry on ECR scoped per arch (type=gha misses on each PR's first push, about 30% of runs). Make it an opt-in input on the shared workflow and canary it on ins-tests. Keep no-cache on the main publish, or add a weekly cache-busting build arg, so OS patches still land. Separately, replace COPY . . + RUN chown -R with COPY --chown in the Dockerfile.
items.risk: The shared workflow serves every repo, so canary first (workspace rule 7). Cached apt layers stop picking up OS patches on branch images until the cache is busted. The ECR build role may need extra permissions for a registry cache.
items.evidence: Stalled runs 39990999718 (apt layer 1992.9s), 39931920617 (1463.9s), 40341880233 (1371.7s), 39857440421 (1091.8s). Normal run 40492746852: apt 20.5s, base pulls 25-30s, export 56-78s. publish-branch p90 21.7 min vs median 3.3. Verdict raised the saving from 1.5 to 3 min: stalls alone average about 189s per run; registry cache would give about 3.5.

items.title: Lighthouse audits 32 pages one after another on one runner, the next-longest PR check
items.current_state: Lighthouse reports about 13.4 min after the push: publish-branch 2.3 min, then the workflow's 11.2 min (stack start 2.0, npm ci 0.6, Run Lighthouse CI 6.2 of which 5.8 is 32 URLs at 10.8s each, teardown 0.5, Pages publish 1.4). Today FIT is the PR's longest check; once FIT is sharded, Lighthouse is.
items.proposal: Split the 32 targets across a 2-way matrix (SHARD_INDEX/SHARD_TOTAL read when slicing targets). Each leg starts its own stack and seeds its own notifications. Upload each leg's report; lighthouse-publish, report-status and flag-simple-findings must merge the two manifests. Do not run two Chromes on one runner: it skews performance scores asserted at minScore 0.6.
items.risk: Saves nothing until FIT is sharded (pt-6); land them together. Each leg adds about 3 runner-minutes. Three consumers of manifest.json need changing. Scores may shift slightly between legs on different runners.
items.evidence: Run 40476571526 (commit d0e429f): 32 'Running Lighthouse' lines at 10.8s each. Runs 40472108338, 40457577904, 40439742721, 40421686703: Run Lighthouse CI 6.1-6.35 min. Same commit: check-pr ended 14.6 min after push, Lighthouse 13.4, e2e about 11. After both changes e2e becomes the critical path at about 11 min.

items.title: E2E shards are unbalanced: one shard runs about 5.8 minutes of tests while the other two run 2.6-3.1
items.current_state: Playwright --shard splits by test count in file order, so on the 'all' scope shard 1 gets the slow animals tests. Run 40484147231: shard jobs 9.0 / 6.1 / 5.8 min with about 3.1 min setup each. The slowest shard sets the wall-clock, and it has grown from about 6 min to 8.5-9 min since 21 Oct.
items.proposal: Weight the existing 3 shards with PWTEST_SHARD_WEIGHTS (read by the installed Playwright), e.g. 2:3:3, so each runs about 3.8 min of tests with no extra runner. A 4th weighted shard gets about 2.9 min per shard for one more runner. A plain 4th shard without weights only saves about 1.5 min, because animals still lands on shard 1.
items.risk: PWTEST_SHARD_WEIGHTS is undocumented and could change between Playwright releases. Fixed weights drift as the suite grows. Same fix as pt-5; one change in the shared workflow serves both. Default-scope callers run fewer tests, so their gain is smaller. Once pt-1 lands, far fewer workspace runs happen.
items.evidence: Run 40484147231 logs: shard 1 '173 passed (5.8m)', shard 2 '181 passed (3.1m)', shard 3 '182 passed (2.6m)'. 12 more runs on 26-27 Oct: one shard 8.0-9.3 min, the others 5.5-6.8. Verdict lowered the saving from 2.5 to 2.0 min for the cheapest fix (weights, 3 shards).

items.title: E2E shard 1 always runs about 2 minutes longer than the other two shards
items.current_state: Count-based sharding gives shard 1 tests/animals/, including the two slowest tests (documents-large-uploads 72s, documents-limits 60s). Run E2E step averages about 302s on shard 1 against 175s and 189s; shard 1 was slowest in every sampled run.
items.proposal: Balance the shards by time in the shared workflow (same change as pt-4: weights on 3 shards, or 4 weighted shards). Moving the two document specs alone saves only about 66s and drifts as tests are added.
items.risk: Lives in the shared workflow, so canary it. Weights drift as tests are added; re-check per-shard step times after a few weeks.

items.title: Frontend FIT tests run 636 Playwright tests on one 4-core runner for 14 minutes, about 2.4 minutes from their own 15-minute timeout
items.current_state: Job median 13.8 min (p90 14.6); test step 10.8-13.4 min. Grew from about 7 min on 31 Aug to 12-14 min since 9 Oct. test:fit:ci sets --global-timeout=900000 (15 min), so the suite will soon fail on its own timeout. It is the PR's longest check.
items.proposal: Make FIT a 3-4 shard matrix: npm run test:fit:ci -- --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ strategy.job-total }} with the blob reporter, upload each blob, and add a merge job running npx playwright merge-reports --reporter html. Keep or raise the global timeout per shard.
items.risk: Low: fullyParallel and isolated stub state. Each shard adds 1-2.5 min of setup (browser install varies). The FIT job itself drops to about 5-6 min, but the PR only gains the overhang over Lighthouse unless pt-3 lands too; together they take all-green from about 14.5 to about 11 min. The bigger reason to do it is clearing the coming global-timeout failure.
items.evidence: Run 40471856356: 'Running 634 tests using 4 workers', '634 passed (12.6m)'. package.json test:fit:ci uses --workers=100% --retries=2 --global-timeout=900000. Six runs: FIT finished after Lighthouse by 0-2.2 min. Verdict lowered the saving from 1.5 to 0.9 min.

items.title: The tests image is pulled cold after the stack is healthy, adding about 50 seconds to every shard
items.current_state: 'Assert E2E stack' takes 47-56s on every shard; almost all of it is docker run pulling the ins-tests image. The pull starts only after 'Start stack' finishes, while the network sits idle for about 56s of health waits.
items.proposal: Start docker pull of the tests image in the background straight after 'Resolve branch tag', and wait on it before 'Assert E2E stack', surfacing a failed pull there. Applies to every caller.
items.risk: Low. Unpacking layers while Java services start may stretch health waits by a few seconds. A failed background pull costs time but cannot break the run, because docker run would pull again.
items.evidence: Run 40484147231 shard 1: stack pulls done 09:53:56, healthy 09:54:52, tests image downloaded 09:55:47. 'Assert E2E stack' 48, 50, 54, 48, 52, 47, 56, 49s across runs 40484147231, 40471919627, 40397371456, 40347454444. Every service repo's e2e gains too; only the workspace's own run rate is counted here.

items.title: Lighthouse is the plants PR's last check to finish and audits its 18 pages one after another on one runner
items.current_state: Lighthouse finishes last on most pushes, about 9.2-10 min after the push, with e2e at about 7.3-7.7. lighthouse-test is 6.4-6.8 min: stack start 1.9, npm ci 0.6, seeding about 0.5, then 18 URLs at about 10s each.
items.proposal: Split the URL list across a 2-way matrix (SHARD_INDEX/SHARD_TOTAL), upload each leg's report and merge manifests and flagged audits in lighthouse-publish. Do the cheap part first or alongside: drop the 0.5 min teardown on an ephemeral runner and fold publish and report-status into fewer jobs (0.5-1 min, no manifest merging).
items.risk: Medium. Report index, flag-simple-findings and report-status all read one manifest.json. A second leg costs about 3 runner-minutes. Gain is capped by e2e; a third leg adds nothing. On pushes where e2e hangs, no gain.
items.evidence: Run 40472136998: 18 'Running Lighthouse 1 time(s)' lines 08:17:21-08:20:18. 13 full pushes 23-27 Oct: Lighthouse finished 1.4-2.8 min after e2e. Verdict kept 1.5 min (range 1.5-1.9).

items.title: Backend PR check reruns on title or description edits and never cancels superseded runs
items.current_state: Triggers include edited; no concurrency group; no paths filter. A title or body edit reruns verify, the Docker build and Sonar (2 jobs, about 6.5-7 runner-minutes). About 3 duplicate runs a week, several 4 seconds apart from tooling that opens then edits a PR.
items.proposal: Drop edited from types. Add concurrency: { group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}, cancel-in-progress: true }. Hold off on paths-ignore until rulesets are checked.
items.risk: Low. No wall-clock gain; duplicates run alongside the real run. Dropping edited also drops reruns on base-branch change, harmless as all PRs target main. Org or repo rulesets not checked.
items.evidence: Same-commit duplicates since 5 Oct: b404e59, 56485a1, d121fab, bc1675d (4 runs), 96afba1, d8496c6, f3d7d53, e34373d. Trigger list unchanged since a4b957e. Saving per run is per avoided run.

items.title: Reference data PRs run the full Maven test suite twice, one after the other
items.current_state: pr-validator runs mvn clean verify (50-71s); sonarcloud waits on it (needs:) and runs mvn -B clean verify sonar:sonar (74-100s), repeating every test. The check takes about 4.5-5 min where one pass would do.
items.proposal: Run the tests once: merge sonar:sonar into pr-validator (checkout needs fetch-depth: 0), or drop needs: so Sonar runs alongside. Keep a plain mvn verify for dependabot, which skips Sonar.
items.risk: Low. Does not make a PR green sooner: publish-branch then e2e (6.5-32 min) finishes later. Dependabot needs its own non-Sonar verify. Runs per week may be nearer 5-13.
items.evidence: Runs 40364495320 (71s / 87s), 40301350048 (69s / 100s), 39582696312 (61s / 89s), 38710039283 (54s / 95s). sonarcloud.yml added in aaf6341 (EUDPA-371), template shape. Verdict saving 1.75 min (stated 2).

items.title: INS frontend FIT tests sometimes stall for 10 minutes downloading Linux packages for the browser
items.current_state: playwright install --with-deps chromium runs every time with no cache or container. Normally about 22s, but in about 8% of runs the apt fetch crawled at about 40 kB/s for 10-11 min, making FIT the PR's slowest check (11-12 min against about 5 min for e2e).
items.proposal: Remove apt from the path: run the job in mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v<pinned>-noble, or drop --with-deps and install the browser only (ubuntu-latest likely has Chrome's libraries; untested). A browser cache alone does not fix it. A step timeout only helps if paired with a retry.
items.risk: Low. Image tag must match @playwright/test. The image pull adds 30-60s each run, off the critical path while FIT finishes before e2e. Saving is lumpy: 6-7 min on a stalled run, 0 otherwise.
items.evidence: Run 40322122844: install 679s, 'Fetched 25.9 MB in 10min 57s (39.5 kB/s)'. Run 39990984344: install 581s. Normal install 16-33s, tests 32-51s. Verdict saving 0.6 min (stated 0.8).

items.title: Plants FIT tests' Playwright install sometimes stalls for 5 to 12 minutes on a slow Ubuntu package mirror
items.current_state: playwright install --with-deps chromium runs apt every time. Normally 0.3-0.5 min; in 7 of 39 runs it took 4.8-12.6 min, pushing FIT past Lighthouse and holding the PR open.
items.proposal: Run the FIT job in the official Playwright container (mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v<version>-noble) and drop the install step; keep the tag in step with package-lock (Dependabot docker entry or a lint check). Caching ~/.cache/ms-playwright does not avoid apt, so it would not fix this.
items.risk: Low. Tag must match @playwright/test. Container changes HOME and user; check port 3053 and artifact paths. Saving is lumpy: 2-5.5 min on about 1 push in 8, 0 otherwise.

items.job: Run Pull Request Checks -> SonarCloud Scan
items.title: INS backend PRs run the whole Maven test suite twice, one after the other
items.current_state: pr-validator runs mvn clean verify (69-85s); SonarCloud waits on it and runs clean verify sonar:sonar again (104-131s). The check takes about 5.3 min. publish.yml repeats the pattern on main, off the image's path.
items.proposal: Drop needs: pr-validator so Sonar runs alongside (saves about 2.2 min of the check). Or merge sonar:sonar into pr-validator (saves about 1.5 min and about 2 runner-minutes). Cover publish-hotfix.yml too.
items.risk: Low. Does not shorten time to all-green: publish-branch then e2e finishes later. Merging means a Sonar outage turns the PR check red. Finding said 8 runs a week; the measured PR run rate is 5, used here.
items.evidence: Runs 40328665442, 39293662509, 38929749587: validator 168-197s, Sonar job 127-139s, workflow about 5.3-5.5 min. needs: copied from animals-backend in e1242b9 (EUDPA-371).

items.title: Address book PR check builds and tests the code twice, one job after the other
items.current_state: pr-validator runs mvn clean verify (44-60s) and a no-cache Docker build; only then does Sonar rerun clean verify sonar:sonar (68-89s). Workflow about 3.5-4.2 min.
items.proposal: Drop needs: pr-validator (saves about 1.6 min, no runner saving) or fold Sonar into pr-validator (saves about 1.3 min and the duplicate test run; needs fetch-depth: 0 and a step-level dependabot guard).
items.risk: Low. Not on the PR's critical path (publish-branch + e2e is longer).
items.evidence: 9 runs incl. 40348122430, 39973069170, 39956822949: pr-validator 1:57-2:43, Sonar 1:27-1:51 starting 2-5s after. needs: copied in 9af238d (EUDPA-371). Verdict saving 1.6 min (stated 1.7).

items.title: INS backend PR check builds the Docker image from scratch, and Publish Branch Image builds it again
items.current_state: 'Test Docker Image Build' runs docker build --no-cache and throws the image away: 63-113s, about 40-55% of the job. Publish Branch Image builds the same Dockerfile on the same PR events, for PRs to any branch.
items.proposal: Remove the step. If a dependabot or fork-PR gap ever matters, keep it only for those PRs with an if: on actor or head repo.
items.risk: Low. Repo has no dependabot.yml and main has no branch protection. Shortens the check and Sonar result, not time to all-green.

items.title: Animals backend main-branch publish runs the test suite after the image is already published
items.current_state: The build job runs 'Build and Publish' (pushes the image), then setup-java and mvn clean verify (126-166s), which gates nothing. publish-arm64 and Sonar wait for it, and Sonar runs clean verify again.
items.proposal: Remove the post-publish setup-java and mvn clean verify steps. Do not move verify before the publish instead: that delays it and saves nothing. Check publish-hotfix.yml for the same step.
items.risk: Low. A red test on main then shows only in the Sonar job; PR checks still gate merges.

items.title: Address book PR check re-builds the Docker image with no cache, which Publish Branch Image already builds
items.current_state: docker build --no-cache runs on every PR push, 52-90s (mean about 70s), the largest step in the job. Publish Branch Image builds the same image on the same events.
items.proposal: Remove the step, or keep it only for dependabot and fork PRs (which the shared publish skips).
items.risk: Low. Dependabot and fork PRs lose their Dockerfile check unless the step is kept for them; no dependabot.yml today.

items.title: Dynamics gateway main-branch publish runs the full test suite again after the image is already published
items.current_state: Build job runs 'Build and Publish' (156-278s), then setup-java and mvn clean verify (160-184s). publish-arm64 and Sonar wait for it; Sonar runs clean verify a third time.
items.proposal: Remove the post-publish setup-java and verify steps. Moving verify before the publish saves nothing.
items.risk: Low. Lose a red build job on main after a bad merge; Sonar's verify still marks the run red. Not checked whether CDP Portal reads the build job's own result.
items.evidence: Runs 39274881696, 39268301322, 37612064198, 37604623358, 37446096353. Workflow from skeleton commit 211bd29. Verdict saving 2.9 min (stated 2.8).

items.title: INS frontend e2e is split over 3 runners that spend most of their time starting the stack
items.current_state: Each shard takes about 3.5 min: stack start 110-144s, assert 48-64s, tests 25-43s. Three stacks run about 1.5 min of tests in total. The k6 smoke job (4.4-5.4 min) is the long pole anyway.
items.proposal: Add a shard-total input to the shared e2e workflow (default 3) and have ins-frontend pass 1.
items.risk: Touches the shared workflow; keep the default at 3. On fast-smoke runs one shard could become the long pole by up to about 30s. Revisit if ins-frontend's suite grows.
items.evidence: 5 runs 23-26 Oct: smoke finished last every time, shards 40-80s earlier. 70 real runs since 13 Oct. About 6-7 runner-minutes per run.

items.title: No concurrency group on the workspace's own PR e2e runs, so superseded pushes keep their shards busy
items.current_state: Service-repo callers cancel superseded runs; the workspace's own pull_request trigger does not. 9 runs in 2 weeks were overtaken while running (about 98 min of overlap, mostly 3 shards each). 5 of 52 runs waited 10-56 min for a runner.
items.proposal: Add concurrency: { group: ws-e2e-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}, cancel-in-progress: true }, gated to this repo's pull_request event. The run_id fallback stops called runs colliding with callers' groups.
items.risk: Low. Cancelling also cancels the older run's report deploy, fine because the newer run publishes to the same path.
items.evidence: EUDPA-296 runs 39997112597 and 39997340816, 98s apart, both ran shards to the 30 min timeout. Queue waits: 40347454444 56.2 min, 40300891423 47.3 min.

items.title: Superseded animals frontend PR pushes keep running the full 14-minute FIT suite
items.current_state: Neither workflow has a concurrency group, so an older push's FIT, unit, Sonar and image builds run to completion. e2e and Lighthouse already cancel. About 4-5 superseded runs a week, mostly from burst pushes.
items.proposal: Add concurrency: { group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true } to both. Keep the Monday schedule run out of cancellation. Skip paths-ignore until required checks are known.
items.risk: Low. Hygiene, not a speed-up.
items.evidence: 18 overlapping runs in 4 weeks, about 131 min of overlap. Earlier 'cancelled' runs (39794171271, 40347856730) were FIT's 20-minute timeout, not this.

items.title: Animals frontend PR checks build the Docker image twice and the frontend bundle twice
items.current_state: pr-validator runs docker build --no-cache (40-52s) while Publish Branch Image builds the same image; build:frontend runs explicitly and again via pretest. Off the critical path.
items.proposal: Keep the Docker step only for dependabot and fork PRs (if: actor is dependabot or head repo differs). Drop the explicit build:frontend line.
items.risk: Low. No required checks on main.
items.evidence: 4 runs: Docker step 40-52s; Publish Branch Image ran 26 of 30, skipped 4 (dependabot/fork guard).

items.proposal: Drop edited from types; add concurrency: { group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }.

items.evidence: atlassian[bot] triggered 39973069170, 39947749545, 39238662827, 39225887695, 38573103388, each 4-5s after the author's run on the same commit.

rejected.reason: Off the critical path: publish then e2e (about 11 min) gates the PR, the check chain ends 3-4 min earlier. Saves about 1.6 runner-minutes per run; safe cleanup, no wall-clock gain.

The work is also larger than stated: the walkthrough CLI rejects --shard and the demo page reads a single results file.

rejected.reason: Walkthroughs finish after FIT in every run, so faster FIT saves no run time. Still a cheap 1-1.5 runner-minute gain if walkthroughs are ever sharded.
